source_text:
Προσωποποιεῖ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις· καὶ
ἐὰν προσωποποιήσῃ τὸν Θεὸν, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Θεὸς ὁ λαλῶν, ἀλλὰ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
ἐκ προσώ-που τοῦ Θεοῦ λαλεῖ· καὶ ἐὰν προσωποποιήσῃ τὸν Χριστὸν, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ
Χριστὸς ὁ λαλῶν, ἀλλὰ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλεῖ.
thought_title: The Holy Spirit personifies in the prophets
orientation: Origen is answering the objection about who speaks in the Psalm by explaining how the Holy Spirit speaks through the prophets.
pass_a_gloss: The Holy Spirit speaks in the person of the prophets; and if it speaks in the person of God, it is not God who is speaking, but the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of God; and if it speaks in the person of Christ, it is not Christ who is speaking, but the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of Christ.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'personifies' for προσωποποιεῖ; it captures the Spirit's act of assuming a person and speaking in that character.
Literal rendering of the prepositional phrase; it preserves the source's spatial metaphor of speaking out of a person.
The glossary requires 'Holy Spirit' and bans 'Holy Ghost'.

choices.term: οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Θεὸς ὁ λαλῶν
choices.english: it is not God who is speaking
choices.why: Keeps the negated copula and the articular participle as a predicate, preserving the source's emphasis on who is not speaking.
rejected: God is not the one speaking

pass_b_english: The Holy Spirit personifies in the prophets. When the Spirit personifies God, God is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks from the person of God. When the Spirit personifies Christ, Christ is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks from the person of Christ.

problems.quote: the Psalm's words are the Savior's
problems.why: Three terms for divine persons shift without mapping; 'Savior' and 'Christ' may be same referent, but 'God' as distinct person is unclear.

problems.quote: the Holy Spirit personifies in the prophets
problems.why: 'Personifies in' is ungrammatical; likely means 'speaks through' or 'assumes person of'.
problems.fix: Revise to 'speaks in the person of'.

problems.quote: the Holy Spirit speaks from the person of God
problems.why: 'From the person of' is opaque; likely means 'in the person of' or 'assuming the role of'.

problems.quote: the Holy Spirit speaks from the person of God
problems.why: Reader may wonder if 'person of God' and 'person of Christ' are different concepts or the same rhetorical device.
problems.fix: Use 'in the voice of God' and 'in the voice of Christ' consistently.

edits.old: The Holy Spirit personifies in the prophets.
edits.new: The Holy Spirit speaks in the person of the prophets.

edits.old: the Holy Spirit speaks from the person of God.
edits.new: the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of God.

edits.old: the Holy Spirit speaks from the person of Christ.
edits.new: the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of Christ.

fixed: Clarified 'Savior' and 'Christ' are the same referent in the work brief; no change needed in this fragment.
Revised 'personifies in' to 'speaks in the person of' for grammatical clarity.
Changed 'from the person of' to 'in the person of' for consistency and clarity.
Used 'in the person of' consistently for God and Christ.

problems.quote: the Psalm's words are the Savior's
problems.why: Three different terms for same figure may confuse reader into seeing distinction.
problems.fix: Use 'Christ/the Savior' consistently or note equivalence.

problems.why: Not true drift, but 'foretold' vs 'speaks' vs 'personifies' are different claims needing clarity.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'foretold' and 'speaks' are same activity, 'personifies' is the mechanism.

problems.quote: When the Spirit personifies God, God is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of God.
problems.why: Paradoxical: God is not speaking, yet Spirit speaks in person of God—needs unpacking.
problems.fix: Add 'i.e., the Spirit assumes God's role/character without being God the Father'.

problems.why: Modern 'personifies' means giving human traits to abstractions; here it means prosopopoeia, speaking in character.
problems.fix: Use 'speaks in the person of' or gloss 'personifies (prosopopoeia)'.

problems.quote: The Holy Spirit speaks in the person of the prophets
problems.why: 'In the person of' and 'personifies' alternate for same concept; reader may miss they are the same idea.
problems.fix: Use one rendering consistently, e.g. 'speaks in the person of' throughout.

variants.text: in the person of the prophets

edits.old: The Holy Spirit speaks in the person of the prophets.
edits.new: The Holy Spirit speaks in the person of the prophets.

edits.old: When the Spirit personifies God, God is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of God.
edits.new: When the Spirit speaks in the person of God, God is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of God.

edits.old: When the Spirit personifies Christ, Christ is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of Christ.
edits.new: When the Spirit speaks in the person of Christ, Christ is not the one speaking; the Holy Spirit speaks in the person of Christ.

fixed: The English already uses 'speaks in the person of' consistently in the first sentence, and the edits now make the rest consistent with that rendering, resolving the glossary and mistranslation concerns about alternating terms.

The unreadable concern about paradox is addressed by the consistent use of 'speaks in the person of', which conveys the prosopopoeia mechanism without needing an explanatory insertion that would stiffen the text.
The glossary concern about 'foretold' vs 'speaks' vs 'personifies' is not present in this excerpt; the English uses only 'speaks in the person of' and 'personifies', and the edits now unify them.
